As of 350 AM Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Stanly Co. has been added to the Heat Advisory for 
today, which otherwise remains in effect for all but the far nrn 
Piedmont counties of cntl NC from 11 AM until 8 PM.

A lower mid-latitude/sub-tropical ridge centered over the srn 
Appalachians has weakened a decameter or two since peaking in 
strength a couple of days ago. It nonetheless will remain in a 
favorable location for excessive heat in cntl NC today, before 
retreating swwd and yielding to lowering heights within a developing 
trough along and just offshore the East Coast through the weekend.
 
Despite the gradually falling heights aloft, the antecedent airmass 
that developed beneath and downstream of it in the low-levels will 
remain in place until eradicated and/or otherwise cooled by a 
frontal passage or widespread convective overturning and outflow. As 
such, it will remain dangerously hot today and have the potential to 
remain so through Sat, though both convective debris cloudiness and 
afternoon convection may limit the magnitude of Saturday's heat. 

Temperatures today should be generally persistence ones, though 
perhaps a degree or two less hot at RDU owing to the 0.42" of rain 
that occurred there from the storm Thu evening (which also notably 
produced a 45 kt wind gust).  When combined with mixed/afternoon 
dewpoints in the upr 60s over the nw Piedmont to lwr 70s 
elsewhere,heat index values will range between 100-105 F over the nw 
Piedmont to mostly 105-109 F in the Advisory area. A couple of 
values near 110 F will be possible at the most reliable observation 
sites from the nrn/ern Sandhills to the cntl Coastal Plain (ie. not 
IXA and CTZ, where values near 115 F will probably result from 
unrepresentative/high-biased surface dewpoints at those sites). 

A canopy of mid-level convective debris cloudiness from the 
(probably weakening) remnants of an overnight convective cluster 
from OH to the Virginias may limit insolation and curb the heat over 
especially the nrn half of cntl NC on Sat. And if that convective 
cluster were to maintain intensity more than currently forecast, 
which they oftentimes do east of the Appalachians, then a more-
prominent cold pool/outflow and possible ongoing convection would 
further limit early day heating there. The airmass will nonetheless 
have the potential to be as hot (or nearly so) as previous days in 
the absence of those lower predictability influences from 
convection/clouds. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... Scattered storms, with a risk of damaging, multi-
cell downbursts, will probably focus across the nrn/ne Piedmont and 
nrn Coastal Plain this afternoon-evening, then possibly throughout 
cntl NC on Sat. However, influences from lower predictability, early 
day convection Sat may hinder storm development or re-
intensification over parts of cntl NC later Sat afternoon. 

Nwly flow around the aforementioned ridge centered over the srn 
Appalachians will gradually strengthen and be accompanied by weakly 
falling heights and cooling through the mid-levels over the srn 
Middle Atlantic through Sat night, as a cyclone progresses across 
Atlantic Canada. 

Meanwhile at the surface, a lee/pre-frontal trough will remain over 
VA/NC, preceding an effective/outflow-reinforced front and trailing 
synoptic one that will gradually settle swd across the OH Valley and 
Middle Atlantic. While both will probably remain to the north of 
cntl NC until late Sat or Sat night, other aggregate outflows will 
probably develop swd across VA and into the nrn Piedmont and nrn 
Coastal Plain of NC through this evening. Indeed, some such outflow 
and related undular bores are evident in KAKQ data this morning 
trailing the MCS now moving offshore the Delmarva. That outflow will 
probably continue to slow, as the parent convection and diabatic 
cooling exit offshore, as it progresses toward the far ne Piedmont 
and nrn Coastal Plain this morning. 

Each of the the surface boundaries noted above will serve as 
possible foci for renewed convective development with strong daytime 
heating. Initially pulse to weakly-organized multi-cells along those 
boundaries may cluster along common outflow while organizing and 
forward propagating sewd across the nrn Piedmont and nrn Coastal 
Plain of NC through this evening, within a belt of 15-25 kts of mid-
level northwesterlies. Continued high DCAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg will 
support a risk of damaging downbursts.

While the environment will similarly sheared and supportive of 
damaging downbursts on Sat, uncertainties regarding the degree and 
location of strongest destabilization cast doubt on where the 
convective focus and severe threat will exist on Sat. Although the 
entire forecast area is in a Slight, Level 2 of 5 risk for severe 
storms, this potential will probably be greatest away from or along 
the differential heating edges of early day convection and debris 
cloudiness, which at this time would favor srn zones for greatest
